---
title: "Grade reports as pairwise decisions"
subtitle: "2.2 · block reading after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), slide 56"
description: "Pairwise statements induced by assigning units to ordered grades."
---

An ordered grade report determines a decision for every pair of units. Pairs in different grades receive a stated
direction; pairs within a grade are withheld. A shared grade makes no assertion of equality between the true values.
The grade labels specify order, with highest priority at the top, rather than numerical distances. Reassigning sites
among the boxes changes the induced pairwise relation. The accompanying matrix records these changes and the totals
of stated and withheld pairs, permitting comparison of reports with different grade sizes and orders.


## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **A, then B to E, then F.** The report states 9 of the 15 pairs and withholds 6, a share stated of .600. Every
  comparison involving either end is stated; the middle grade withholds its internal pairs. Moving a middle site into an end grade changes the outlined matrix cells.
- **Three grades of two sites.** The same number of grades now states 12 of the 15 pairs and withholds only 3,
  a share of .800. Each grade withholds its own internal pair. Disclosure depends on the sizes as well as the number of grades.
- **Four sites: 1/2/2/2.** The smaller report states 3 of the 6 pairs, a share of .500. A focused site button accepts a destination grade number. Enter selects the site, arrow keys specify a destination, and a second Enter completes the move. The dashed
  boxes create a new grade at either end.
- **Beyond letter order.** The report {B, D} > {C, F} > {A, E} still states 12 of the 15 pairs. Any grouping and
  ordering can be built. The blue and orange transposed cells represent the same unordered pair: each stated pair appears in both triangles,
  while the pair count includes it once.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
These fictional after-school sites are ordered for practice-documentation visits, with no funding consequence.
The matrix represents the supplied report without evaluating the accuracy of its directions. Empty grades
disappear after a move, preserving the relative order of the occupied boxes.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
postrank_evaluate(c(A=1L,B=1L,C=2L,D=2L,E=3L,F=3L), pr_tutorial$one, weights=c(score_A=1), tau=.2)$N # 12
canonical_postrank_grade(c(A=3L,B=3L,C=7L,D=7L,E=9L,F=9L), LETTERS[1:6]) # 1 1 2 2 3 3
```
:::

Standalone: [report builder](../../embed/report-builder.html), for example `?units=6&grades=3,1,2,1,3,2`.
